text: Cloudways Review (2026): Managed Cloud Hosting, Real Costs, Pros and Cons By Michael @ Expertah Updated November 2026 11 min read Disclosure: we may earn a commission if you buy through links on this page, at no extra cost to you. It never changes our verdict. How we review The short version Cloudways gives you a managed cloud server for WordPress, WooCommerce and PHP apps without having to run the server yourself. Prices start at $14 a month for a 1 GB DigitalOcean server, billed monthly for what you use, with no long contract and a 5-day free trial that needs no credit card. It’s noticeably faster and more flexible than shared hosting, and much cheaper than premium managed WordPress hosts. The trade-offs: it costs more than shared hosting, backups, email and some security tools are billed extra, and there’s no cPanel. It’s best for growing sites, stores and agencies that have outgrown shared hosting. Try Cloudways free → Most people start on shared hosting, where hundreds of sites share one server. When your site gets busier, or you start selling online, that setup starts to show its limits (see our best ecommerce hosting guide for how store hosting differs). Cloudways is one of the most popular next steps: you pick a cloud provider and server size, and Cloudways sets up and looks after the server for you. Here’s how Cloudways works, what it really costs once you add the extras, and who it suits. We checked prices and features on Cloudways’ website in November 2026. What is Cloudways? Cloudways is a managed cloud hosting platform owned by DigitalOcean. Instead of selling you space on its own servers, it launches a server for you on a big cloud provider (DigitalOcean, Vultr, Linode, Amazon Web Services or Google Cloud) and handles the setup, security patches, caching and monitoring. You manage your websites from Cloudways’ own dashboard. It now sells four products. Flexible is the classic Cloudways platform most people mean, with a server you size yourself. Autonomous is fully managed WordPress hosting that scales automatically for busy stores and learning sites. Cloudways also lists Velocity and an AI Agents product. This review focuses on Flexible, with a look at Autonomous. Plans and pricing Plan (DigitalOcean Premium) RAM / vCPU NVMe storage Bandwidth Price per month Micro 1 GB / 1 25 GB 1 TB $14 Small 2 GB / 1 50 GB 2 TB $28 Medium 4 GB / 2 80 GB 4 TB $54 Large 8 GB / 4 160 GB 5 TB $99 Prices in US dollars from Cloudways’ pricing page, checked November 2026, before tax. These are the default DigitalOcean Premium servers; Vultr, Linode, AWS and Google Cloud are priced differently, and AWS and Google Cloud prices vary by region. Every plan allows unlimited websites and visits, limited only by what the server can handle. Billing is pay-as-you-go. Cloudways tracks usage by the hour and sends one invoice on the 1st of each month for the month before. If you change plans halfway through a month, you pay each plan for the days you used it. There are no annual contracts, though you can add credit to your account in advance if you prefer to prepay. Autonomous is priced differently: $99 a month (Growth), $199 (Scale) or $399 (Plus) for one website, with autoscaling, Cloudflare Enterprise CDN, Object Cache Pro, malware protection and unlimited off-site backups included. Extra disk space is $1 per GB and extra bandwidth $0.04 per GB, plus an hourly charge if traffic spikes push it beyond its baseline servers. It has a 3-day free trial. What you’ll really pay The server price isn’t the whole bill. These are the extras most people end up paying for: Extra Cost Off-site backups $0.033 per GB (about $0.50 per 15 GB) Business email (Rackspace) $1.50 per mailbox a month Cloudflare Enterprise CDN From $4.99 per domain a month Malware protection From $4 per app a month Extra bandwidth $0.02 per GB on DigitalOcean and Linode, more on AWS and Google Cloud Advanced support $100 a month Tax Added in some countries For example, one small WordPress site on the Micro server with about 10 GB of backups and two email accounts costs roughly $17 to $18 a month . A WooCommerce store on the Medium server with Cloudflare Enterprise and malware protection comes to about $63 a month before email. That’s more than shared hosting, where a first-year deal can be $3 a month, but there are no renewal price jumps: the price you see is the price you keep paying. Features Lightning Stack: Cloudways’ server setup with built-in caching for WordPress and PHP apps. Object Cache Pro and Redis: included for free; Object Cache Pro is enabled on 4 GB servers and above, and Cloudways says it normally costs $95 a month. Staging and cloning: create a staging copy of a site, test changes and push them live with one click. Automated backups: scheduled or on-demand, with one-click restores (storage billed per GB). Security: a server firewall (Imunify360), bot and brute-force protection, free Let’s Encrypt SSL and a WordPress vulnerability scanner. Free migration: Cloudways’ engineers move your first website for free from any host. Developer tools: SSH and SFTP, multiple PHP versions, Git and a built-in database manager. What you don’t get is cPanel or included email. Cloudways uses its own dashboard, and email is a paid add-on through Rackspace. Domain registration also isn’t included, so you’ll buy your domain elsewhere. Performance and scaling Your sites run on a server with dedicated resources rather than sharing one with hundreds of other accounts, and Cloudways uses NVMe storage and server-level caching. In practice, that is the main reason people move to Cloudways: busy WordPress sites and WooCommerce stores, which can’t rely on page caching alone, usually run more smoothly on a dedicated cloud server than on cheap shared hosting. When you need more power, you can scale the server up from the dashboard. You can also pick the cloud provider and data center closest to your visitors, from more than 50 locations. If you expect sudden traffic spikes, such as flash sales or course launches, Autonomous adds automatic scaling, load balancing and failover, at a much higher price. Ease of use Cloudways is easier than running a server yourself, but it isn’t as simple as a beginner shared host. You launch a server, then add applications such as WordPress or WooCommerce to it, and manage server settings and site settings in separate parts of the dashboard. Things like pointing your domain, setting up email and adding SSL take a few more steps than on hosts that bundle everything. If you’re comfortable with WordPress and a little technical, it won’t take long to learn. If you want a host that handles your domain, email and website in one place, a shared host like SiteGround or Hostinger is simpler. Our guide to choosing a web host explains the difference. Support and billing Support: 24/7 live chat and tickets on every plan, plus email. Help with plugins, themes and performance tuning needs the Advanced Support add-on ($100 a month). Free trial: 5 days on Flexible with no credit card, using DigitalOcean, Vultr or Linode. The server is deleted at the end unless you add a payment method. Refunds: we didn’t find a money-back guarantee on Cloudways’ pricing page; the free trial is the way to test it before paying. Payment: Visa, Mastercard, American Express or PayPal. Cancelling: delete your servers and paid add-ons to stop billing; you get a final invoice for usage up to that day. Things to know before you sign up It costs more than shared hosting. Expect $14 to $18 a month for a small site once backups and email are added. Backups and email are extra. Budget for both. No cPanel, no free domain. You’ll use Cloudways’ dashboard and register your domain elsewhere. AWS and Google Cloud cost more and vary by region; DigitalOcean, Vultr and Linode are the better value for most sites. Basic support covers the server, not your plugins or theme, unless you pay for Advanced Support. Not keen on managing a server, even a managed one? If you run WordPress and want backups, malware removal and email included without choosing server sizes or paying for add-ons, WPX is the simpler option. It is WordPress-only, with less room to scale than Cloudways, but every plan includes daily backups, free malware cleanup and done-for-you migrations. Its Black Friday sale runs until December 7. Who is Cloudways a good fit for? A good fit if you… Pros have outgrown shared hosting run a WooCommerce store or busy WordPress site want to pay monthly with no renewal price jumps manage several client sites as an agency want to choose your cloud provider and location are comfortable with a little technical setup Look elsewhere if you… Cons are building your first small site on a tight budget want email and a domain included want cPanel need a money-back guarantee want fully hands-off support for plugins and themes Our take: Cloudways is one of the best-value ways to move up from shared hosting. You get a fast, managed cloud server for a fraction of what premium managed WordPress hosts charge, with monthly billing and no renewal surprises. Just budget for the extras. Use the Cloudways WordPress setup for blogs and business sites, or Cloudways for WooCommerce for stores. For more options, see our guides to the best WordPress hosting and best WooCommerce hosting , or compare premium managed hosts in Kinsta vs WP Engine . Our verdict Cloudways is a strong choice for growing WordPress sites, WooCommerce stores and agencies: dedicated cloud resources, good caching tools, monthly billing and a free trial with no card. It isn’t the cheapest option for a small first site, and backups, email and advanced support cost extra. Try Cloudways free → Cloudways for WooCommerce → Want everything bundled instead? Rocket.net vs Cloudways compares the real monthly cost once you add Cloudways’ extras, and our Rocket.net review covers it in full. Frequently asked questions Is Cloudways good for beginners? It’s manageable if you’re comfortable with WordPress, but it takes more setup than shared hosting. Beginners building a first small site are usually better served by a shared host that includes email and a domain. How much does Cloudways cost? Flexible plans start at $14 a month for a 1 GB DigitalOcean Premium server, billed monthly for what you use. Off-site backups ($0.033 per GB), email and some add-ons cost extra. Autonomous starts at $99 a month. Does Cloudways have a free trial? Yes. Flexible has a 5-day free trial with no credit card needed, on DigitalOcean, Vultr or Linode. Autonomous has a 3-day trial. Does Cloudways include email? No. Business email is available through Rackspace for $1.50 per mailbox a month. Is Cloudways good for WooCommerce? Yes. Dedicated server resources, Redis and Object Cache Pro help stores with lots of products and logged-in shoppers. A 2 GB or 4 GB server is a sensible starting point for most stores. Can I cancel Cloudways any time? Yes. There’s no contract; delete your servers and add-ons to stop billing, and you’ll get a final invoice for usage up to that point. text: We pay for the servers and plans we use. The links go straight to the vendors; no vendor pays us for them today, and that never changes what we recommend. Details . Our earlier Cloudways articles were read from the pricing page. This one is not: on 4 October 2026 we started the free trial, launched the cheapest server Cloudways sells, installed WordPress and timed the things you would actually use: page speed, a staging copy, a backup and a restore. Tested 4-5 Oct 2026: one Cloudways account on the free 3-day trial; one server (DigitalOcean, Frankfurt, Basic Standard 1 GB: 1 vCPU, 25 GB SSD, 1 TB transfer, shown as $11/month or $0.0154/hour after the trial); WordPress (latest) with the "Optimized" Lightning stack and MariaDB 10.11; a fresh site with the default theme and no plugins. Speed was measured with curl from a laptop on another continent and from our own server in DigitalOcean Frankfurt. One site, one day, no load test: treat the numbers as a fair snapshot, not a benchmark of every plan. The 2-minute video version: Cloudways review, the $11 server timed (YouTube) . What we measured Test Result How we measured Page speed, same city, from cache 0.083 s median (0.069 min, 0.178 max) 20 requests from our DigitalOcean Frankfurt server Page speed, same city, no cache 0.282 s median (0.256 min, 0.932 max) 10 requests with a unique query string, so the page cache could not answer Page speed, from another continent 0.582 s median (0.561 min, 1.656 max); first request 3.374 s 20 requests from a laptop on another continent Staging copy (same server) Between 3 min 25 s and 4 min 11 s Clicked "Launch Staging Application" at 00:04:22; ready at the 00:08:33 check On-demand backup Under 1 min 32 s (backup stamped 12 s after the click) "Take Backup Now" at 00:13:20; "Backup completed" by 00:14:52 Full restore Between 48 s and 1 min 31 s "Complete Restore" at 00:15:52; finished between 00:16:40 and 00:17:23; the site answered 200 afterwards Server launch More than 5 minutes; not timed exactly The dashboard logged us out mid-launch, so we only have bounds: still building at 5 min 15 s, running when we checked again 27 minutes later The response headers explain the fast cached numbers: every page came back with x-cache: HIT from Varnish, which Cloudways switches on by default. The uncached figure (282 ms) is the honest one for logged-in users, carts and anything personalised. What the trial looked like No card. Starting the trial asked for nothing beyond the existing login. The banner said billing only starts when you upgrade, and the trial ends 3 days after the first server launches. Choices on the way in: application (WordPress, WooCommerce, PHP, Laravel, Magento), cloud (DigitalOcean, Vultr, Linode, AWS, Google), region, database (MariaDB or MySQL) and server size. It pre-selected a 4 GB Premium server at $54 a month; we had to switch to Standard and slide down to 1 GB to get the $11 plan, so check the summary before you launch. Panel on the 1 GB plan: SSH and SFTP access (with your own SSH keys or a terminal in the browser), monitoring, service management, PHP and package settings, security, vertical scaling, backups and SMTP for the server; staging, backups, cron jobs, SSL, Git deployment, Cloudflare and migration tools for each app. One warning worth knowing: when we created the staging copy, Cloudways advised a server of 4 GB or more if you run several PHP versions per app. On 1 GB, keep sites on one PHP version. Admin login: Cloudways created the WordPress admin with the account's email address as the username. Change it if you would rather not expose that. Who should buy it, and who should not Good fit: you run WordPress sites for yourself or clients and want staging, one-click backups and restores, SSL and a support desk without touching a server. The $11 plan handled a fresh site comfortably; staging and restores take minutes, not an afternoon. Poor fit: you are comfortable with a terminal or a self-hosted panel. The same 1 GB DigitalOcean droplet costs about half as much bought directly, and tools like Coolify give you deploys and backups on it ( our side-by-side , and what each cloud costs on Cloudways ). Before you pay: use the 3-day trial the way we did. Launch the same size you plan to buy, restore a backup once and time a staging copy. Those three things tell you whether the panel saves you real time. Start the free Cloudways trial Limits of this test One fresh WordPress site with no traffic, one server size, one region, one day. Every Cloudways server ships with: - **Nginx** as the web server (not Apache) - **Varnish** full-page cache with configurable TTL - **Memcached and Redis** for object caching (Object Cache Pro included since Q4 2025) - **PHP 8.3** with OPcache tuned out of the box - **HTTP/2** enabled by default; HTTP/3 available on Cloudflare CDN add-on We compared identical WordPress installs (same theme, plugins, content) across three providers: | Metric | Vultr HF ($16/mo) | DigitalOcean Premium ($14/mo) | AWS Small ($38.56/mo) | |---|---|---|---| | TTFB (uncached) | 48 ms | 89 ms | 62 ms | | Fully loaded (GTmetrix) | 0.9 s | 1.3 s | 1.1 s | | PageSpeed (mobile) | 94 | 88 | 91 | | LCP | 1.2 s | 1.8 s | 1.4 s | Vultr HF wins on raw speed. DigitalOcean Premium is the budget pick that still performs well. AWS only makes sense if your business already runs AWS infrastructure and needs same-region hosting. **The performance gotcha nobody mentions:** Cloudways' Varnish cache purges on every WooCommerce order by default. On high-traffic stores processing 50+ orders per day, this creates cache-miss spikes. The fix: set Varnish exclusion rules for `/cart/`, `/checkout/`, and `/my-account/` paths while keeping product and category pages cached. You can run PHP 8.3 on one app and PHP 8.1 on another within the same server. - **Staging**: One-click push-to-staging with a URL you can share with clients for approval. Pull changes back to production when ready. We used this on every client project. - **Backups**: Automated daily backups with 1-click restore. On-demand backups before risky plugin updates. Backup frequency adjustable to hourly on higher plans. - **Git deployment**: Connect a Git repo and deploy via push. This works well for theme and plugin development workflows. - **Server scaling**: Vertical scaling (upgrade RAM/CPU) takes about 2 minutes with no data loss. For the WPSchool audience — small business owners and freelancers building WordPress sites — Cloudways on Vultr HF offers the best performance-per-dollar. Cloudways doesn't offer a formal uptime guarantee with credits like Kinsta does. If uptime SLA enforcement matters to your business, that's a factor worth weighing — though in practice, the actual uptime numbers are competitive. ## Who Should Use Cloudways (And Who Should Skip It) **Cloudways is the right pick for:** - **Freelancers and agencies** managing 5–30 client WordPress sites who want one dashboard, pay-as-you-go billing, and the ability to spin up or tear down servers per project - **WooCommerce store owners** processing under 500 orders/day who need fast checkout pages without WP Engine or Kinsta pricing - **Content publishers** running high-traffic blogs where Varnish + CDN delivers sub-second page loads - **Developers** who want SSH access, Git deployment, and configurable PHP/server settings without managing the OS layer **Skip Cloudways if:** - You've never managed a WordPress site before and want true hand-holding (Kinsta or [SiteGround](/comparisons/hostinger-vs-siteground/)'s managed WordPress plans are more beginner-friendly) - You need email hosting bundled with your web hosting ([SiteGround](/comparisons/siteground-vs-bluehost/) includes email; Cloudways doesn't) - You run WordPress multisite networks (WP Engine supports this natively) - Your budget is under $14/month ([Hostinger](/reviews/hostinger-review/) or shared [SiteGround](/reviews/siteground-review/) plans start lower) **Our final rating: 4.3 out of 5.** Cloudways earns top marks for performance, flexibility, and value — docked for missing email hosting, no managed WordPress updates, and inconsistent tier-1 support quality. Cloudways works for beginners comfortable with a 20-minute learning curve. The dashboard replaces command-line server management but lacks cPanel-style features like a file manager and email setup. Total beginners should consider SiteGround's managed WordPress plan at $17.99/month. ### How much does Cloudways cost per month? Configure Varnish exclusion rules for cart and checkout pages to avoid cache-related order issues. ### How does Cloudways handle WordPress security? AWS: enterprise projects, global scale, widest service ecosystem. Google Cloud: big data and machine learning integration. For most WordPress sites, Vultr HF 2GB ($32/mo) offers the best value. Is it hard to migrate from shared hosting to Cloudways? No. Cloudways offers a free migration plugin. You can transfer your WordPress site with a single click. While the panel is different, WordPress management works as you are used to. The key difference is the server concept: on Cloudways you first create a server, then deploy an application (site) on it — shared hosting does not have this separation. Does Cloudways require a contract? No. Cloudways uses hourly billing — no commitment, cancel anytime. There is a monthly billing cycle, but charges stop as soon as you discontinue. You can start with a 3-day free trial (credit card required). Does Cloudways offer a staging environment? Yes. Staging is available on all plans. You can clone your live site with one click, test changes, and push to production when ready. Git integration also allows you to set up a CI/CD pipeline. What is the difference between Cloudways and Kinsta? Both are managed cloud hosting but take different approaches. Cloudways: 4 infrastructure options, lower starting price ($14/mo), more server control, multi-application support. Kinsta: Google Cloud only, higher price (from $35/mo), easier interface, WordPress only. Technical users tend to prefer Cloudways, while those who want simplicity lean toward Kinsta. How many data centers does Cloudways have? Cloudways offers 65+ data center locations across 4 infrastructure providers — spanning North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, South America, and Oceania. This means you can place your server close to your target audience for optimal latency. What is Cloudways' refund policy? Cloudways does not offer a traditional money-back guarantee. Instead, it provides a 3-day free trial (credit card required). After the trial, billing is hourly with no long-term commitment — you only pay for what you use and can cancel at any time. text: Quick answer Cloudways earns a 4.4/5 for agencies: unbeatable cost-per-site on Vultr HF, solid Redis caching, and more infrastructure control than any other managed WordPress host at this price. Cloudways is the managed WordPress host I recommend to most agencies managing 5+ client sites. Not because it's the fastest — Rocket.net 's edge caching beats it for cached TTFB. Not because it has the best support — Kinsta 's engineers are stronger. But because Cloudways gives you more control over your infrastructure than any other managed host, at a price point that makes per-site economics work at scale. This review is based on direct experience running client sites on Cloudways for over three years, across multiple server options and regions. What Cloudways actually is Cloudways is a managed hosting platform layered on top of major cloud providers. You choose the infrastructure; Cloudways manages the server setup, security patching, and software stack. Current infrastructure options: DigitalOcean — the most popular option, good price/performance Linode (Akamai) — solid alternative to DigitalOcean Vultr — includes Vultr High Frequency (NVMe SSD), the performance option AWS — for clients who need AWS infrastructure Google Cloud Platform — for clients who need GCP This infrastructure choice is Cloudways' biggest differentiator from Kinsta, Rocket.net, and WP Engine. You can pick DigitalOcean for budget client sites, Vultr HF for performance-sensitive sites, and AWS for enterprise clients — all from the same dashboard. The managed stack on every server: Nginx web server Varnish Cache (full-page caching) Redis object cache (€14/month add-on, not included) PHP-FPM (multiple versions, switchable per app) MariaDB Let's Encrypt SSL, auto-renewed Automated daily backups One important clarification: Redis is not included in Cloudways' standard pricing. It is a €14/month add-on. This is a meaningful cost difference from Hetzner + CloudPanel (where Redis is included free) and should factor into your total cost calculation for WooCommerce stores with heavy session usage. Performance benchmarks Results from the WordPress Hosting Speed Test 2026 : Cloudways Vultr High Frequency 2GB (NVMe): Metric Result Cached TTFB (EU) 32ms Uncached TTFB 165ms Lighthouse Performance 96 LCP 1.4s Cloudways DigitalOcean Premium (NVMe): Metric Result Cached TTFB (EU) 38ms Uncached TTFB 190ms Lighthouse Performance 95 LCP 1.5s The Varnish Cache on Cloudways produces strong cached TTFB — 32ms on Vultr HF is competitive with most managed hosts. Uncached performance at 165ms is solid. Rocket.net's edge caching beats it on cached TTFB (18ms), but Cloudways beats Rocket.net on uncached performance for WooCommerce stores. Pricing Cloudways pricing is based on server size and provider — you pay for the underlying cloud server, plus Cloudways' management fee. Multiple WordPress sites can run on a single server (no per-site cost within a server tier). DigitalOcean servers: Server RAM vCPU Storage Price/mo DO 1GB 1GB 1 25GB SSD €11 DO 2GB 2GB 1 50GB SSD €22 DO 4GB 4GB 2 80GB SSD €42 DO 8GB 8GB 4 160GB SSD €80 Vultr High Frequency (recommended for performance): Server RAM vCPU Storage Price/mo Vultr HF 1GB 1GB 1 32GB NVMe €13 Vultr HF 2GB 2GB 1 64GB NVMe €25 Vultr HF 4GB 4GB 2 128GB NVMe €49 For agency use — practical server recommendations: 1–3 low-traffic sites: Vultr HF 1GB (€13/mo) 5–10 mixed sites: Vultr HF 2GB (€25/mo) — this is my standard recommendation 10–20 sites with some WooCommerce: Vultr HF 4GB (€49/mo) High-traffic WooCommerce or busy client portfolios: Vultr HF 8GB (€96/mo) Add Redis for WooCommerce stores (€14/mo per server). This applies to the whole server, not per site — so if you have 5 sites on one server and need Redis for one WooCommerce store, that's €14/mo total, not €14 per site. Features Multi-cloud infrastructure is Cloudways' strongest feature for agencies. You can have: Budget client sites on DigitalOcean 1GB A performance-focused e-commerce client on Vultr HF 4GB An enterprise client who specifically requires AWS All managed through the same Cloudways dashboard. Team access and permissions. Cloudways has team member access controls with role-based permissions. Add developers to specific applications without giving them server-level access. Essential for agencies delegating work. Per-application staging. Every application (WordPress site) gets a staging environment at one click. Clone production to staging, test, push changes. Staging uses the same infrastructure as production — no surprises. Application-level settings. PHP version, PHP memory limits, file size limits, and caching settings are configurable per application from the UI — not via SSH. Useful for managing mixed environments where one plugin requires PHP 8.1 and another needs 8.3. Cloudways Bot — automated vulnerability detection that flags outdated plugins with known CVEs across your server. Useful for agencies doing maintenance retainers. Cloudways CDN — available as an add-on (Cloudflare-powered), not as included Cloudflare Enterprise like Rocket.net. Fine for static assets; does not provide edge HTML caching. Getting started: what setup actually looks like Most reviews skip the part you'll actually spend your first afternoon on, so here it is in order. You launch a server first, then applications on top of it — that two-layer model is the thing that confuses people arriving from cPanel hosting, where a "site" is the only unit. Choosing a provider (DigitalOcean, Vultr HF, Linode, AWS, GCP), a size, and a region takes about five minutes, and the server is provisioned in roughly ten. Adding a WordPress application to that server takes another two. The practical consequences of that model matter for agencies: You size the server, not the site. Ten small brochure sites on one €25/month Vultr HF 2GB is the normal arrangement, and it's where the cost advantage comes from. Vertical scaling is one click , but it restarts the server. Scale during a maintenance window, not during a client's campaign launch. Applications share server resources. A runaway process on one site can affect its neighbours — the trade-off you accept for the price. Put a client's high-traffic store on its own server rather than beside nine other sites. You get SSH and SFTP access, WP-CLI, and Git deployment. If you're used to a fully locked-down managed host, that access is the main day-to-day difference: when something breaks at 11pm, you can actually get in and look, and our WP-CLI and functions.php snippets are usable here in a way they aren't on more restrictive platforms. Backups and restore This is the section that should decide the purchase for anyone hosting client sites, and it's the one most Cloudways reviews omit entirely. Automated backups are configurable per application , with frequency options from hourly through weekly, plus retention settings. You can also take an on-demand backup before a risky deployment — which should be reflexive before any plugin update on a client site. Restore is per-application , not all-or-nothing at the server level. That matters: restoring one client's site shouldn't roll back the nine others sharing that server. Two caveats worth knowing before you commit: Backup storage is billed separately from the server, per GB. It's inexpensive, but on a server holding a dozen media-heavy sites with hourly backups it's a real line item rather than a rounding error. Check the frequency you've set against what you're paying. Local backups still live on the same infrastructure. For client work under contract, keep an off-site copy as well. Our backup plugin roundup covers the options for pushing a second copy somewhere independent, which is what you want when the failure mode is "the provider had a bad day", not "I broke the site." Security Cloudways handles the server layer competently, and it's worth being precise about where its responsibility stops. Included: dedicated firewalls on every server, free Let's Encrypt SSL with auto-renewal, two-factor authentication on the platform account, IP whitelisting for SSH and SFTP, and OS-level patching handled by Cloudways rather than you. Cloudways Bot flags outdated plugins with known CVEs across the server, which is genuinely useful on a maintenance retainer where you're tracking dozens of sites. Not included: anything above the server. WordPress-layer hardening is yours — admin credentials, plugin hygiene, file permissions, login protection. Our security hardening checklist is the companion piece here, and there's no hack-fix guarantee of the kind Kinsta includes, so budget for cleanup yourself using our hacked site process if it ever comes to that. The honest framing: Cloudways secures the server so you don't have to, and leaves WordPress to you. That's the correct division for an agency that knows what it's doing, and a gap for one that assumed "managed" meant "someone else worries about the plugins." Migrating to Cloudways Cloudways provides a free migration plugin that handles the standard case — install it on the source site, enter the destination details, and it moves files and database across. For a normal blog or brochure site this genuinely works without drama. Coming from SiteGround specifically? Our SiteGround to Cloudways migration guide covers the SiteGround-only plugins and email that need handling. Where it needs help: multisite networks, sites with unusual server-level configuration, and very large media libraries where a plugin-based transfer times out. Cloudways also offers migration assistance from their team, and it's worth asking rather than fighting the plugin on a complicated site. The sequencing advice from our WordPress migration guide applies here as it does anywhere: drop DNS TTL to 300 seconds a day ahead of the cutover, verify on the staging URL before switching, and use maintenance mode to hold writes during the window so you don't lose form submissions against the old server. One Cloudways-specific step people miss: after migration, configure Varnish exclusions before you send traffic , not after. The default cache rules will happily cache pages they shouldn't on a WooCommerce site, and the symptom — customers seeing each other's carts — is the kind of bug you want to find on staging. Billing, trial, and support in practice The trial is genuinely free. Three days, no credit card required, which is enough to launch a server, migrate a real site to it, and run your own benchmarks rather than trusting anyone else's. If you're evaluating hosts, do exactly that — our hosting speed test methodology is reproducible on a trial server. Billing is pay-as-you-go and hourly , not annual contracts. You're billed for what the server runs. The agency-relevant consequence is that spinning a server up for a client project and destroying it when the project ends costs you only the hours used — a genuinely different economic model from prepaid annual plans, and one that suits project work well. Support is chat and ticket, with no phone option. Base support is included; faster response tiers are paid add-ons. In practice, response times of 5–15 minutes are normal for straightforward server questions, and the agents are competent on infrastructure. They are not WordPress engineers in the way Kinsta's are — a question about a plugin conflict or a WordPress-specific performance problem will get you a polite boundary rather than a diagnosis. Know which kind of problem you're buying support for. What Cloudways doesn't do well Redis is an add-on, not included. €14/month on top of server cost. For WooCommerce stores, Redis object cache is important for session management and performance under load. You should budget for it. Varnish Cache requires WooCommerce exclusion configuration. Out of the box, Varnish will cache WooCommerce pages it shouldn't (cart, checkout, logged-in users). Cloudways provides exclusion settings but you need to configure them correctly. Misconfiguration causes cart/checkout bugs. For a full breakdown of caching options and WooCommerce edge cases, see best WordPress caching plugins . No phone support. Support is chat and ticket-based. Chat response is typically 5–15 minutes. For agencies managing client sites on SLA, this matters — Kinsta's support is more responsive for complex WordPress issues. Pricing isn't always cheaper. At the high end of the server range, Cloudways can approach or exceed Kinsta pricing per site, without Kinsta's isolation guarantees (Cloudways puts multiple apps on one server). The economics are best in the €25–€50/month server range for 5–15 sites. Cloudways vs Kinsta The most common comparison for agencies: Feature Cloudways Kinsta Infrastructure Multi-cloud (choice) Google Cloud C2 only Site isolation Shared server Isolated containers Cached TTFB 30–40ms 55–80ms Uncached TTFB 165–190ms 160ms Redis €14/mo add-on $100/mo add-on CDN Add-on Cloudflare CDN included Support Chat, 5–15 min Chat/ticket, WordPress engineers 10-site pricing ~€49/mo (Vultr HF 4GB) ~€115/mo (Business 1) Pick Cloudways if: you want infrastructure control, manage a mix of site types, or are cost-sensitive at scale. Pick Kinsta if: you need site isolation guarantees, GCP infrastructure, or the best WordPress-expert support. See Cloudways vs Kinsta for the full comparison. Who Cloudways is right for Agencies managing 5–20 client sites. This is the core case and the one the pricing model is built for. Ten sites on a €25/month Vultr HF 2GB server is an economic structure no per-site managed host can match, and the per-application staging and team permissions are what make it workable across a team rather than just cheap. Developers who want access. SSH, WP-CLI, Git deployment, and per-app PHP version control mean you can work the way you'd work on your own VPS, without running the VPS. If you've ever been blocked by a managed host's restrictions at an inconvenient moment, this is the feature you're buying. Project work with a defined end. Hourly pay-as-you-go billing makes spinning up a server for a three-month build and destroying it afterwards genuinely cheap. Mixed portfolios. Budget sites on DigitalOcean, a performance client on Vultr HF, an enterprise client who insists on AWS — one dashboard, one invoice. Who should look elsewhere Anyone who needs guaranteed isolation. Applications share a server. If a client's contract requires that their site's performance cannot be affected by anything else, Kinsta 's container isolation is the honest answer, and the wider alternatives field covers the rest. Content sites with a global audience. Varnish serves from your one server's region. Rocket.net 's Cloudflare Enterprise edge caching at 18ms is a fundamentally different architecture for globally distributed readers. Agencies that want WordPress-level support. Cloudways support is competent on infrastructure and stops at the WordPress boundary. If you want to escalate a plugin conflict to someone else, you want Kinsta. Single-site owners who want it handled. The server/application model and the Varnish configuration are overhead that only pays off across a portfolio. One site, no technical appetite — this isn't the product. Verdict Cloudways is the best value managed WordPress host for agencies in 2026. The Vultr HF 2GB server at €25/month handles 8–12 WordPress sites with Nginx + Varnish caching, and the per-app staging and team access controls are better than most premium hosts. The €14/month Redis add-on is the main cost surprise — budget for it on any server hosting WooCommerce stores. And note that cached TTFB (32ms) is good but not Rocket.net-level (18ms) for global audiences. For agencies where server economics matter, Cloudways runs 10 sites at roughly a quarter the cost of Kinsta, with comparable performance in most real-world scenarios. It's not the fastest host available, but the combination of performance, server control, and price makes it the best overall value for agencies. How many WordPress sites can I run on Cloudways? A Vultr HF 2GB server ($26/month) comfortably handles 8–10 medium-traffic WordPress sites with Redis object caching and Cloudflare in front. Heavier sites with WooCommerce should be limited to 3–4 per server. Does Cloudways include Redis? Redis is available as a paid add-on on Cloudways — it's not included by default. At around $12/month per server it's worth enabling; it significantly reduces database load and improves TTFB for repeat visitors. What cloud providers does Cloudways support? Cloudways supports DigitalOcean, Vultr, Linode, AWS, and Google Cloud. For most agency use cases, Vultr High Frequency offers the best performance-to-price ratio. What is Cloudways' main weakness? Cloudways charges extra for Redis, email hosting, and some support tiers.
